chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fish that is caught, then placed in something, then returned to the water, so it dies in it. He said: 'Do not eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fish that are caught, put in a container, and then returned to the water where they die?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for fish that are caught, removed from their natural habitat, and then returned to the water to die, declaring them impermissible to eat. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between fish that die while still in the water (which are generally considered halal) and those that die out of water or are removed and then die, emphasizing the condition of being 'alive in water' at the time of death for lawful consumption.
